The Past Perfect with other Time Expressions
You can use the Past Perfect with different time expressions to talk about events that happened prior to other events in the past.

You can use the Past Perfect with time expressions like:
  • as soon as
  • immediately
  • the moment
    • As soon as I had finished my research assignment, I emailed it to my professor.

This shows that the action in the Past Perfect time clause was completed before the main clause action happened.
  • until/ till
  • before
    • Before I had chosen a topic for my research assignment, I discussed possible ideas with my professor.

With before, the Past Perfect action will always come after the action in the Simple Past.
  • I talked about several ideas with my friends also until/ till I had decided on what to write.

With the time expressions until/ till, the action in the Past Perfect may come after the action in the Simple Past.
  • You can also use the Past Perfect in both clauses of a sentence.
    • The research assignment took a lot of time and effort. Before I had written anything, I had spent about 10 hours doing research.
The moment she had seen the woman was half eaten up by rats and ants, she took her to the hospital.
Before they had brought a staff of doctors and nurses provide medical care for these people, they had had nowhere else to go.
Reason and Result Clauses
You sometimes have to provide reasons for why something happens, and the results for when it does. You can use special conjunctions to show this in your sentences.
You use the conjunctions as/ because/ since at the beginning of a clause when you want to introduce the reason for something.

Example:
I was feeling sick at work. I asked my boss if I could go home at lunchtime.
Why did you go home? What was the reason?
As/ Because/ Since I was feeling sick at work, I asked my boss if I could go home at lunchtime. (note the use of the comma if the reason clause comes before the main clause)
I asked my boss if I could go home at lunchtime as/ because/ since I was feeling sick at work.
You can also use as/ since/ seeing that with the meaning “in view of the fact that”.

Example:
As/ Since/ Seeing that I did all the cooking, you could wash the dishes.
You could wash the dishes as/ since/ seeing that I did all the cooking.
If you want to use as/ since/ seeing that in reference to information that was said before or understood, you can use if also.

Example:
Lana: I don't want to go to the cinema later.
Adam: As/ Since/ Seeing that/ If you don't want to go the cinema later, can we watch a movie home instead?
You can also use if so.

Example:
Lana: I might go to the beach on Sunday.
Adam: If so, don't forget to check the weather. I read that there may be rain on Sunday.
(meaning: If you go to the beach on Sunday, don't forget to check the weather.)
You can also express results with so and therefore. Therefore is a little more formal.

Examples:
I was feeling sick at work, so I asked my boss if I could go home at lunchtime.
I was feeling sick at work. Therefore, I asked my boss if I could go home at lunchtime.
As the building had been empty, he asked me if I wanted it.

images.text:
Mother Teresa first became famous because she did so much charitable work. She started this work in Calcutta even before she had opened the Home for the Dying Destitutes.
In the book Something Beautiful for God, Mother Teresa described the first time she picked up a dying woman from the street and how she opened the home.
The moment she had seen the woman was half eaten up by rats and ants she took her to the hospital. Unfortunately, they hadn't been able to do anything for her. They had only taken the woman in because Mother Teresa had refused to go home unless something was done for her. As soon as they had taken her, Mother Teresa had gone straight to the town hall. She asked for a place where she could take these people, because she had found more people dying in the street.

The employee at health services had brought her to the temple so he  could show her where the pilgrims used to rest after they worshipped the goddess Kali. As the building had been empty, he asked her  if she wanted it. Seeing that Mother Teresa was very happy with the building, the official had been pleased. Immediately they had brought in the sick and suffering. They had started the Home for the Dying Destitutes. Before they had brought a staff of doctors and nurses in to provide medical care for these people, they had had nowhere else to go. They hadn't had anyone to care for them.

Although almost half of those brought to the home died, they were given the chance of dying with dignity, and not in shame. Those who did recover were helped to find jobs and a place to live.
There are now homes for the dying all over India and in many other places around the world. Mother Teresa and the Sisters of Charity have set a noble example for caring for the needy.
